Stage 2 already has a modern receipt, date-stamped. On June 12, 2026, the US Commerce Department told Anthropic it needed a license before its two most capable models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5, could reach any foreign person anywhere, after researchers reported a way around the models' safeguards that produced working exploit code. [Mayer Brown, Commerce Department Extends Export Controls to Advanced AI Models](https://www.mayerbrown.com/en/insights/publications/2026/06/commerce-department-extends-export-controls-to-advanced-ai-models-authorizes-release-to-specific-trusted-partners) The company couldn't block only foreign users on short notice, so it switched both models off for everyone, worldwide. Within days a Chinese lab, Z.ai, published an open-weight model under an MIT license, its model card promising "no regional limits, technical access without borders." [Z.ai, GLM-5.2 model card](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.2) The people who wrote the directive weren't stupid, any more than the people who wrote the Red Flag Act were. They were doing what an incumbent with a legal pad can do to a machine that's already loose: deciding where it lives, while telling themselves they were deciding whether.

Then Stage 3 arrived on schedule. After two and a half weeks of negotiation, Commerce lifted the controls on June 30, in exchange for commitments to detect and address security risks, report malicious activity, and work with the government on standards for future models. Access began returning the next day. [Al Jazeera, US lifts restrictions on powerful AI models](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/7/1/us-lifts-restrictions-on-powerful-ai-models-fable-mythos-anthropic-says) Panic to paperwork in eighteen days. That's the whole arc of this chapter, run at speed, with receipts.
